ACT · STUDY GUIDE

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023

Criminal procedure: information, investigation, production, search, seizure, electronic processes, and trial.

2023 · in force 1 July 202412 explained sections
Official full textPrint guide
Use the applicable version and state notifications. Electronic processes do not remove authentication, signature, or other safeguards.

Understand the provision.

Original plain-language explanations. The official text controls.

BNSS · 94

Summoning production of documents or things

Broadly succeeds CrPC section 91. A qualifying authority may require production of a necessary or desirable document or thing, including electronic records, subject to the provision and exclusions.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 105

Audio-video recording of search and seizure

Provides mandatory recording for specified searches using mobile phone or other electronic means, with the stated progression toward implementation. Check the current notification and read with section 185.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 106

Attachment of property from criminal activity

Provides a mechanism concerning proceeds of crime in specified circumstances, with approval and notice requirements. It is not a general shortcut to confiscation without procedure.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 173

Information in cognizable cases

Broadly succeeds CrPC 154 and expressly addresses electronic communication, signature within the specified period, and information by a woman for specified offences. Subsection (3) adds a preliminary-enquiry mechanism for certain offences and conditions.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 174

Investigation of cognizable cases

Addresses investigation of cognizable cases and specified forensic procedures for serious offences, including audio-video documentation. Establish applicability and practical implementation.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 180

Examination of witnesses

Broadly succeeds CrPC 161. Record the examination accurately and follow the signature, recording, and other safeguards in the applicable provision.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 183

Confessions and statements

Broadly succeeds CrPC 164. The magistrate, recording method, warnings, signature, and forwarding requirements must be followed. A forensic examiner does not acquire this power merely by expertise.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 185

Search by police officer

Broadly succeeds CrPC 165, with expanded recording and audiovisual-search provisions. Record grounds, scope, things sought, and execution in accordance with the current text.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 193

Police report

Broadly succeeds the investigation-report function of CrPC 173. Track the statutory report, further investigation, and specified communication duties using the current section numbering.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 528

Inherent powers of the High Court

Broadly corresponds to CrPC 482. It preserves specified inherent powers to prevent abuse of process or secure the ends of justice, subject to legal limits.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 530

Electronic mode of proceedings

Provides for specified trials, inquiries, and proceedings by electronic means. Implementation, rules, and the nature of the proceeding must be checked; it is not an unconditional virtual-trial entitlement.

Verify in the official text
BNSS · 534

Repeal and savings

Contains the transition from the CrPC. Determine how pending investigations, proceedings, and earlier actions are saved rather than applying a simple date-only rule to every procedural question.

Verify in the official text
